idea.problem: Fix three confirmed defects in Coin's internal SbHash<Key,Type> chained hash table (broken const-only iterator, a self-assignment that clears the source before copying it, and a resize that is not exception-safe and leaks live objects when a key/value copy throws mid-rehash) and decide whether resize should relink existing nodes instead of copying them, informed by how mature hash table implementations handle the same problems.
users: Coin maintainers hardening SbHash (internal, COIN_INTERNAL-only container used by 40 files)
capabilities: guard copy assignment against self-assignment as the first statement, before any destructive mutation
publish a rehashed table's new bucket array only after its allocation succeeds, without destroying any existing node on the failing path
relink existing nodes into new buckets during resize instead of copying and destroying every key and value
reduce a hash value to a bucket index using a prime bucket count with plain modulo instead of a power-of-two mask
apply an avalanche/mixing step to a hash value before reducing it to a bucket index
constraints: C++11 as the minimum supported language standard
must not require heap allocation beyond the bucket array and node pool already in use
non_goals: switching the storage strategy away from chained buckets
changing the container's public method names
